author: t. c. leon
title: Andy Chan says AI is increasing value of liberal arts for graduates
text:
Wake Forest University Vice President for Innovation and Career Development Andy Chan said on Apr. 29 that artificial intelligence is raising the importance of a liberal arts education as the Class of 2026 approaches graduation.
The topic is significant as concerns about AI’s impact on jobs have grown, but Chan argues that students with a liberal arts background are well positioned to succeed in an AI-enabled workforce. He said, “AI is actually resurrecting the value of a liberal arts education.”
According to Chan, the National Association of Colleges and Employers has rated the job market for new graduates in 2026 as “fair,” marking the first neutral rating since 2009. Despite initial conservative forecasts, employer confidence has improved, with NACE’s Job Outlook 2026 Spring Update showing hiring projections revised upward by 5.6% compared to last year.
Chan also addressed common misconceptions about hiring timelines for new graduates. He pointed out that data shows a “spring surge” in hiring: “37% of full-time hiring for this class is happening now, with a wave of ‘just-in-time’ hiring expected to continue through the summer.”
At Wake Forest University, career engagement begins at orientation and continues throughout students’ academic journey. The university offers ongoing personal and career development support for alumni at every stage.
Chan said he can provide strategic insights into these trends and share stories from students navigating current job market conditions or alumni who have benefited from Wake Forest’s programs.
